AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: Brimstone.cs:19-30 applies PowerVar<StrengthPower>('SelfStrength', 2m).BaseValue to the owner with applier = the owner, then PowerVar('EnemyStrength', 1m).BaseValue to every living opponent with applier = NULL. brimstone.py:22-24 does both in the same order with the same amounts and the same applier discipline -- `applier=player` for the self application and no applier kwarg for the enemies. The null applier is not incidental: relic/unsettling_lamp's doubling requires `applier is self.player`, so an applier-carrying enemy Strength here would create a Lamp interaction that does not exist in the game. The slot is right (post-draw AfterSideTurnStart = on_player_turn_started, executed via the turn-order probe), and note there is NO turn guard on either side -- Brimstone fires every turn, unlike most of this batch.

guards.what: N1: C# targets `GetOpponentsOf(owner).Where(c => c.IsAlive)` (Brimstone.cs:25-27); the sim uses Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:294-297), which filters on `not e.is_gone`
guards.rationale: `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py), so the sim's filter is if anything STRICTER than C#'s IsAlive -- it also excludes an escaped-but-alive creature, which C#'s GetOpponentsOf would have already dropped from the combat's opponent list. Distinct from relic/bag_of_marbles' G2, where the C# side used HittableEnemies (IsAlive AND Hook.ShouldAllowHitting) and the sim's weaker filter let an unhittable enemy be targeted: here C# asks only for IsAlive, so there is no ShouldAllowHitting clause to lose. Worth the entry precisely because the two relics look identical at a glance and only one of them is a gap.

guards.what: N2: the self-Strength is applied BEFORE the enemy Strength on both sides
guards.rationale: Order matters if any listener reacts to a Strength application by changing a later one; both codebases apply self first (Brimstone.cs:24 then :28; brimstone.py:22 then :23-24). Recorded because the two applications differ in applier, and swapping them would change which is visible to relic/unsettling_lamp's latch.

The `player != base.Owner` / `shuffler == base.Owner` / `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player. The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState), so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N4: Flash() and the Strength hover tip (Brimstone.cs:17, 23)
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
